{{Short description|Pareto efficiency implies utilitarian rule}}{{Electoral systems sidebar}}{{Economics sidebar}}

In [[decision theory]], the '''Harsanyi's utilitarian theorem''' proves mathematically that a rational [[social welfare function]] that satisfies the expected utility axioms and respects the [[Pareto principle|Pareto indifference principle]] must be a weighted sum of individuals' [[utility functions]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Risse |first=Mathias |date=2002 |title=Harsanyi's 'Utilitarian Theorem' and Utilitarianism |jstor=3506225 |journal=Noûs |volume=36 |issue=4 |pages=550–577 |doi=10.1111/1468-0068.t01-1-00401 }}</ref>

==Theorem==

===Assumptions===
#The society (or group) is [[Rational agent|rational]] and maximizes expected [[social welfare]].
#Each individual in the group is rational and maximizes his individual's expected [[utility]].
#If every individual in the group is indifferent between two [[probability distributions]], then the group as a whole is indifferent as well.

===Statement===
[[John Harsanyi]], through this theorem, proves that a [[social welfare function]] that satisfies these three assumptions, would be the weighted sum of expected individual utility functions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ben_West🔸 |date=2020-02-20 |title=Harsanyi's simple "proof" of utilitarianism |url=https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/v89xwH3ouymNmc8hi/harsanyi-s-simple-proof-of-utilitarianism |access-date=2026-07-17 |website=Effective Altruism Forum}}</ref>

Mathematically, the social welfare function <math>W</math> social welfare function <math>W</math> can be represented as a linear combination of individual utilities:<ref>{{cite book |last=Hammond |first=Peter J. |chapter=Harsanyi’s Utilitarian Theorem: A Simpler Proof and Some Ethical Connotations |date=1992 |title=Rational Interaction: Essays in Honor of John C. Harsanyi |pages=305–319 |editor-last=Selten |editor-first=Reinhard |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer  |doi=10.1007/978-3-662-09664-2_17 |hdl=1814/371 |isbn=978-3-662-09664-2 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mandler |first=Michael |date=July 2005 |title=Harsanyi's utilitarianism via linear programming |journal=Economics Letters |volume=88 |issue=1 |pages=85–90 |doi=10.1016/j.econlet.2004.10.017 }}</ref><math display="block">
W(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i u_i(x) + c
</math>

where:

* <math>u_i(x)</math> is the von Neumann–Morgenstern (vNM) utility function of individual <math>i</math>.
* <math>a_i</math> is the weight assigned to individual <math>i</math>, reflecting the individual's contribution to social welfare.
* <math>c</math> is a normalization constant, that does not affect the ordering of social preferences.
